- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative or near zero (e.g., sentiment < 0.3) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in price correction: model often lags true price movements by 2–4 days, especially after sharp turns — adjust forecast to align with recent 3–5 day trend.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, pushing prices away from recent 10-day average — use 10-day moving average as a constraint.
- High sentiment + high forecast = overconfidence — reduce forecast by 5–10% if sentiment > 0.7 and price is rising.
- Low sentiment + low forecast = underconfidence — increase forecast by 5–10% if sentiment < 0.3 and price is falling.
- Avoid extrapolating from 18-day history — true price often deviates from 30-day trend; use 10-day rolling average for smoother forecasting.
